in: Migration: one diary table; three columns on creator pitches (rounds per side, who countered last); a factual backfill marking existing counters as brand-sent, since nobody else could have sent one
Diary writers on all six steps. An entry records WHAT CHANGED (15% -> 22%), not that something did. The shoot keeps its existing record AND writes here.
One server-side step calculation — what step a collaboration is on and whose turn it is, track-aware
One server-side needs-you count — per collaboration, set, campaign and tab; a parent equals its children plus its own
New route: the creator counters back on her own pitch, validated by the same rules the other direction uses, under the same admin-set round limits
Correction 1: brand acceptance settles the LATEST terms, whoever moved them last
Correction 2: the brand's counters on a pitch are capped at the same rounds the creator has (unbounded today)
Correction 3: nobody can accept their own counter — the check must look at WHO countered, not just that someone did
out: Any screen in any app. Zero files under Packages/* are touched.
Backfilling old history. The diary starts the day it ships; what was overwritten is gone, and inventing it would put fiction on a screen two people use to settle disagreements.
The brand's pitch settings screen — that is Phase 1.
Rendering the step number or the needs-you count anywhere — Phases 2 and 4.

why_this_phase_is_first: Five later phases read from it. The history screens in FINAL 1 panel 8 and FINAL 4 level 5 cannot be built over four steps that keep no history. And if either app ever computes the step number or the needs-you count itself, the brand's screen and the creator's screen will eventually disagree about the same collaboration — the exact failure the whole spine exists to prevent.

verification.written_as: things to try, not test names
fail_first_required: T19 brand acceptance settles the latest terms
T20 the brand's counters are capped

verification.fail_first_rule: Each correction gets a check written first, failing, then the fix. A check written after the fix proves only that the code does what it does.
verification.assert_rule: Assert what comes back in the response, not what the query does. A diary entry computed and then dropped by a serialiser is a feature that does not exist — that has happened in this repo before.
verification.headline: A negotiation from last month can be read back in full, by both parties, showing every offer that was ever on the table — and a creator can name her own price on her own pitch. Neither sentence is true today.

flagged_risks.diary_write_must_not_fail_its_action: A diary write that throws must never take down the action it was recording. A missing history line is a nuisance; a counter that did not send because its history line failed is a defect.
flagged_risks.two_writers_for_the_shoot: The shoot keeps its existing record and also writes to the diary. Two writers for one truth is normally a smell; accepted here because the existing record is load-bearing for the admin production queue. If they ever disagree, the diary is wrong.
flagged_risks.diary_shape: It must carry six kinds of event without becoming a shapeless bag. If a rejection reason or a parcel shortfall does not fit cleanly, widen the shape now rather than migrate again in Phase 7.
flagged_risks.pre_handshake_records: A handful of collaborations predate the handshake and have no negotiation to record. Their step number needs an agreed answer rather than a silently chosen one — will come back to the founder rather than pick.
flagged_risks.invisible_phase: Nothing is visible, so nothing is obviously broken. This phase can only be proven by reading data back. If the checks are weak it ships unverified and surfaces in Phase 2 as a screen showing the wrong thing.
